This is a review article discussing ventilatory depression and residual effects of anesthetics. It does not involve sugammadex and is not an RCT.

This is an overview article providing general knowledge on neuromuscular blocking agents. It does not involve sugammadex and is not an RCT.
This is a systematic review about grey literature in meta-analyses. It does not involve sugammadex and is not an RCT on sugammadex.
This is a methodological study about detecting bias in meta-analyses using funnel plots. It does not involve sugammadex and is not an RCT on sugammadex.

This is a randomized trial where 17 adult patients (20-81 yrs, ASA 1-2) randomly received different doses of sugammadex (1.0, 2.0, 4.0, 6.0, 8.0 mg/kg). This meets the criteria as it compares different doses of sugammadex in adult patients.
This is an observational case-control study assessing TOF ratios in patients with critical respiratory events vs controls. It does not involve sugammadex and is not an RCT.
This is a prospective observational study about complications and mortality following anaesthesia. It does not involve sugammadex and is not an RCT.

This is a randomized Phase II dose-finding study where 50 adult patients were randomized to receive different doses of sugammadex (0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0, or 8.0 mg/kg). This meets the criteria as it compares different doses of sugammadex in adult patients.

This is a randomized study where 30 adult patients received randomly assigned doses of Org 25969 (sugammadex) (0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0 or 6.0 mg kg−1). This meets the criteria as it compares different doses of sugammadex in adult patients.
This appears to be a review/commentary article discussing previous findings about residual paralysis. It does not involve sugammadex and is not an RCT.

This is a randomized, safety-assessor-blinded study where 84 adult surgical patients (ASA class I–III) were randomized to sugammadex 2.0 mg kg−1 or neostigmine 50 µg kg−1. This meets the criteria as it compares sugammadex with another medication in adult patients.
This is an RCT comparing rocuronium, succinylcholine, and vecuronium for rapid-sequence induction. However, it does not involve sugammadex, so it does not meet the selection criteria.
This is an animal study conducted in dogs. It does not involve human adult patients or sugammadex, so it does not meet the selection criteria.
This is a case report presenting a single patient case with pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic modeling. While it involves sugammadex, it is not an RCT, so it does not meet the selection criteria.
This is a survey study assessing the incidence of postoperative residual curarisation following atracurium or vecuronium. It does not involve sugammadex and is not an RCT.
This is a methodological paper about a statistical test for publication bias in meta-analyses. It does not involve sugammadex and is not an RCT.

This is a randomised, multicentre, parallel-group trial including 98 adult subjects (age≥18 years, ASA class 1 to 3) who received either sugammadex 2.0 mg kg−1 or neostigmine 50 μg kg−1. This meets the criteria as it compares sugammadex with another medication in adult patients.
This is an observational study assessing residual curarization in 64 PACU patients who received vecuronium or pancuronium. It does not involve sugammadex and is not an RCT.
